facts.raw_span: A 45-year-old man
history of systemic lupus erythematosus, well controlled without immunomodulatory therapy
a 30 × 20 mm painless, slowly progressive mass on his left forehead over 1 year
excision of a similar frontal bone lesion diagnosed as fibrous dysplasia 2 years earlier
denied headaches or neurologic symptoms
the lesion showed a ground-glass appearance with homogenous matrix expansion of the frontal bone, predominantly affecting the external cortex
Fine-needle aspiration cytology with immunostaining excluded multiple myeloma (no CD138+ cells)
a core biopsy demonstrated diffuse sclerosis, complete bone resorption, and intra-trabecular fibrosis; the bone was not uniformly mineralized
these findings were reported as suggestive of fibrous dysplasia
Preoperative laboratory tests, including inflammatory markers, renal function, and blood counts, were within normal limits
the patient underwent complete surgical excision of a 40 × 50 mm portion of frontal bone, including the lesion with a 15 mm margin of normal bone
the bone defect was repaired with an autologous calvarial graft using piezoelectric osteotomies
